data.description:
# `verify.overlap_enabled` does not say what it overlaps, what it costs, or that it is advisory

## What the setting actually does

When enabled, running a plan review ALSO performs store-wide duplicate detection on the reviewed
ticket. Three stages (`llm/overlap/wire.py:overlap_findings`):

1. an LLM digests the ticket (`ticket-digest`, `llm/enrich.py`);
2. BM25F keyword retrieval finds similar tickets across the WHOLE tracker, excluding the query
   ticket's own graph (`llm/overlap/retrieve.py`, `graph.related_ticket_ids`);
3. an LLM judges each surviving candidate PAIR (`llm/overlap/judge.py:judge_one`).

It surfaces at most 3 candidate `duplicates` / `supersedes` / `depends_on` link suggestions in a
separate `overlap[]` verdict key. It is ADVISORY: it never blocks a claim and never affects the
claim-gate verdict. Default off. Introduced by epic only-crave-art.

## Why the name should change

`overlap_enabled` fails to convey four things a reader needs at the config line:

1. **Overlap of WHAT.** "Overlap" alone could mean code, schedules, responsibilities, time windows.
   It means cross-TICKET duplicate/supersede/dependency relationships.
2. **That it is STORE-WIDE.** The retrieval stage scans the whole tracker, so the work scales with
   store size rather than with the ticket under review. Nothing in the name hints at that.
3. **That it is ADVISORY-ONLY.** Sitting under `verify.` alongside genuinely blocking gates
   (`require_plan_review_for_claim`, `require_ticket_for_commit`) actively suggests it might gate
   something. It cannot.
4. **That it rides on `review-plan`.** A reader looking for what a plan review does would not think
   to check a key named `overlap_enabled` under `verify.`.

## Recommended name

**`verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`** — names the OUTPUT (link suggestions), which is the thing an
operator is actually deciding whether they want. `suggest_` also carries the advisory nature, which
`_enabled` does not. Alternatives considered: `cross_ticket_duplicate_detection` (accurate but says
nothing about being advisory), `advisory_overlap_detection` (keeps the ambiguous "overlap").

## The documentation gap, which is the more concrete defect

**The setting is documented NOWHERE outside the config-schema docstring.** A grep across `docs/`
for `overlap_enabled` and for "store-wide overlap" returns nothing. For an opt-in feature that
performs LLM work proportional to tracker size, the absence of a `docs/config.md` entry is the part
most likely to cost someone real money or confusion.

## Measured context, so the cost is a fact rather than an impression

From a real `rebar review-plan` run on this repo with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` enabled, aggregated by
token rather than by call count (call count alone is a poor cost proxy — a cheap model doing many
calls may cost less than one expensive call):

    op                                 calls   input_tok   % of review input   model
    overlap-judge                         18       37,560               65.0%   claude-opus-4-8
    plan-review-verifier                   1        7,182               12.4%   bedrock sonnet
    plan-review-prerequisite-verifier      1        3,990                6.9%   bedrock sonnet
    plan-reviewer                          1        3,795                6.6%   bedrock sonnet
    ticket-digest                          1        3,138                5.4%   claude-opus-4-8
    plan-review-coach                      1        2,152                3.7%   bedrock sonnet
    TOTAL                                 23       57,817

So the overlap step is **~65% of a plan review's input tokens**, and `cache_read_tokens` was **0**
on every row. Note it currently runs on `cfg.model` (the frontier-class default) only because of
bug `afeb`, which routes these sub-calls through the class vocabulary; once that lands the same
work should be materially cheaper. **This ticket is about NAMING and DOCUMENTATION, not cost** — the
numbers are here so whoever writes the docs entry can state the cost shape accurately.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the setting is renamed to a name that states what it produces, with the old name still
      accepted as a deprecated alias so no existing project config breaks
- [ ] the deprecation path follows this repo's existing convention for renamed config keys (see how
      `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` was handled in ticket d23e — the standing decision there was `_scheduled`,
      not `_permanent`, because the six `_permanent` precedents are RENAMES rather than
      supersessions; a rename here should match whichever of those two patterns applies)
- [ ] `docs/config.md` documents it: what it does, the three stages, that it is advisory and never
      blocks, that its work scales with tracker size, and which model class each stage uses
- [ ] every in-repo reference to the old name is updated (config schema, any tests, any docs)
- [ ] a test asserts the deprecated alias still resolves, so an existing project config keeps working

## Notes

Filed UNPARENTED at the operator's direction: renaming is approved but is out of scope for epic
061c (the LLM provider seam). Discovered while measuring which calls in a plan review ignore the
model-class configuration (bug `afeb`).
data.title: Rename verify.overlap_enabled to name what it produces, and document it (it is currently undocumented outside the config schema)
